Article Title: IndiGo aircraft hits parking stand pole at Srinagar airport
Article Text:
Srinagar: Ground staff attend to an IndiGo aircraft after flight 6E 225 (VT-NOG), operating from Navi Mumbai to Srinagar, hit a pole while being parked at Srinagar airport (PTI Photo).

MUMBAI: An IndiGo aircraft operating from Navi Mumbai to Srinagar came into contact with a parking stand pole while parking at Srinagar International Airport on Friday, shortly after landing. The aircraft departed Navi Mumbai at 6.50am and landed in Srinagar at 9.25am.IndiGo, in a statement, said all passengers and crew were safe and had deplaned from the aircraft. The relevant authorities were immediately informed, and an investigation is underway. The aircraft has been grounded for necessary maintenance and will resume operations after securing the required clearances.
Article Summary: An IndiGo aircraft operating from Navi Mumbai to Srinagar came into contact with a parking stand pole. All passengers and crew were safe and had deplaned from the aircraft. The aircraft has been grounded for necessary maintenance and will resume operations after securing the required clearances.

Article Title: PM Modi congratulates 'friend' Meloni on becoming longest-serving postwar Italian PM
Article Text:
PM Modi congratulates Italian PM Giorgia Meloni

Poll Vote & Share your view Are you optimistic about the future cooperation between India and Italy under Meloni and Modileadership? Yes, very optimistic Not optimistic 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday congratulated his Italian counterpart Giorgia Meloni, a day after she become Italy's longest continuously serving prime minister since the post- World War II era.In a post on X, PM Modi said the milestone reflects Italian people's confidence in Meloni."Congratulations to my friend Prime Minister Meloni on becoming the longest continuously serving Prime Minister in Italy's postwar history. This milestone is a reflection of the trust and confidence of the Italian people in her leadership," the prime minister wrote."Her friendship has also been instrumental in advancing the India-Italy Special Strategic Partnership and I look forward to continuing our close cooperation to build a prosperous future for the people of our countries. My best wishes for her continued success in the years ahead," he added.The two leaders' widely known friendship is often referred to as "Melodi" - a combination of their surnames.Meloni, who has served as Italy's prime minister since October 2022, is the first woman to hold that position.On Thursday, her conservative administration marked 1,413 uninterrupted days in office, making it Italy's longest-serving continuous government since World War II and surpassing the record previously set by late former Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi from 2001 to 2005.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi congratulates Italian PM Giorgia Meloni on her 1,413 days in office. PM Modi said the milestone reflects Italian people's confidence in Meloni. Meloni has served as Italy's prime minister since October 2022, the first woman to hold that position.

Article Title: 'Will always face consequences': Yogi Adityanath warns 'anti-national' forces
Article Text:
Anti-national forces harming India's unity will face consequences: Adityanath

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Friday warned that anti-national and anti-social forces seeking to spread hatred or undermine India's unity would face consequences, invoking Lord Krishna's message on the occasion of Janmashtami.Addressing a gathering in Mathura, the birthplace of Lord Krishna, on the second day of his visit, Adityanath emphasised that His teachings and message remained equally relevant today."Wherever the forces of goodness exist, they will be protected under all circumstances. But wherever anti-national and anti-social forces raise their heads, create hatred in society or attempt to harm India's unity, integrity and faith, Lord Krishna had already said 5,000 years ago what their fate would be," PTI quoted the chief minister as saying.Yogi Adityanath also cited the Bhagavad Gita's teaching, "Paritranaya sadhunam, vinashaya cha dushkritam" (for the protection of the righteous and destruction of evil), stressing that it continued to guide society.The chief minister highlighted the Braj region's role in preserving its religious heritage and the memories of Lord Krishna despite repeated invasions and attempts by various groups to impose their faith on India."Many invasions took place and many people tried to impose their faith on India, but no one could erase the Sanatan faith," Yogi Adityanath said."Those who dared to erase Sanatan faith themselves disappeared into the dust, but the memories of Shri Krishna and Radha Rani, not only in Braj but across India, continue to inspire us today and provide an encouraging environment for future generations," he added.The chief minister welcomed devotees arriving in Mathura for Janmashtami and extended his greetings to the people of Uttar Pradesh on the festival marking the birth of Lord Krishna.Yogi Adityanath has been in Mathura since Thursday for Janmashtami celebrations and has been attending programmes ahead of the festival.
Article Summary: Yogi Adityanath: Anti-national forces harming India's unity will face consequences. Uttar Pradesh chief minister was in Mathura, the birthplace of Lord Krishna. He said Lord Krishna had already said 5,000 years ago what their fate would be.

Article Title: Watch: 2 workers make it out alive 9 days after Nepal floods hit hydropower tunnel
Article Text:
The rescue of two workers have revived hope for hundreds of others still said to be trapped

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be prioritized in Nepal's recovery plan? Infrastructure rebuilding Financial aid for affected families Long-term disaster preparedness Environmental restoration 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Rescuers in Nepal pulled two workers alive from a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydropower project on Friday, nine days after devastating floods and landslides trapped hundreds of workers inside tunnels across several hydropower sites.The rescue brought a dramatic breakthrough to a desperate operation, but hopes of finding more survivors rose further after rescuers heard voices coming from inside the tunnel, according to Bipin Regmi, police chief in the flood-hit district of Nuwakot.“Rescuers heard voices,” Regmi told CNN, adding that a medical team was on its way to the site.The two workers were pulled out in quick succession from inside the Trishuli 3A plant, where rescuers have been boring into a tunnel in an effort to reach 42 workers who had remained unaccounted for.Video showed about a dozen rescuers pulling one man through a small opening in the ground and clapping as he emerged. The mud-covered worker was then carried away on a rescuer’s shoulder, while a medical team checked on him.Nepal Army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet confirmed the first rescue during the operation. Nepal lawmaker Shri Ram Neupane later said a second worker had also been rescued alive.The tunnel leading to the underground powerhouse is more than 4 kilometres (2.5 miles) long.Dozens of workers were inside when the catastrophic flooding hit the area.About 900 workers are missing from 12 hydropower projects in Nepal, according to local authorities, with roughly 500 believed to be trapped inside tunnels. Among those unaccounted for are workers from China, South Korea and India.Read more: Nepal estimates $2.56 billion flood damage, faces $52.6 million recovery cost The rescue effort has continued under treacherous conditions since Aug. 26, when massive floods and landslides tore through parts of Nepal, likely after a glacier collapse. At least 1,259 people have been killed and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to Nepal’s disaster management agency.On the Tibet side of the border, China said late Wednesday that 21 people had been killed and 541 were missing.The chances of finding survivors have become increasingly uncertain with each passing day. Indian Army Colonel Parikshit Mehra, who was involved in the rescue operation at the Trishuli 3A site, said earlier this week that the first 48 hours are the most crucial in a tunnel rescue.“People who are stuck tend to panic much more than when they are outside in the open,” Mehra told CNN’s Anderson Cooper.“Getting stuck in a tunnel you can’t see anything. Generally if you stay in the dark you get disoriented in about 24-25 hours,” he said.“Beyond that, (after) 48 hours, you start hallucinating. And then I think from there on it’s always a fight.”Yet, even as the operation entered its ninth day, Mehra offered a note of hope saying, “There have been miracles.”Also read: Nepal minister goes back on flash flood 'compensation' claim The flash floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, caused widespread destruction across northern and central Nepal, killing at least 1,282 people and leaving thousands missing. Nepal Police said the highest number of recovered bodies were reported from Chitwan, Nawalparasi East and West, Nuwakot and Rasuwa, with rescue and recovery operations continuing across the affected areas.
Article Summary: Rescuers pulled two workers alive from a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydropower project on Friday. The rescue brought a dramatic breakthrough to a desperate operation, but hopes of finding more survivors rose further. At least 1,259 people have been killed and more than 5,000 remain missing.

Article Title: ‘Hit him because he was speaking wrong’: Ganesh mandal worker after slapping anti-noise activist in Pune
Article Text:
An anti-noise campaigner was assaulted on Tilak Road in Pune

Poll Vote & Share your view Should the use of high-decibel sound systems during Ganeshotsav be banned? Yes No 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





PUNE: Anti-noise campaigner Vidyanand Bapat of Narayan Peth was assaulted on Tilak Road on Thursday allegedly by a member of a Kothrud-based Ganesh mandal, amid a simmering debate over the use of DJs and high-decibel sound systems during Ganeshotsav.The accused, identified as Santosh Chavan, president of Kothrud-based Janjagruti Pratishthan, was taken into custody soon after the incident. The Vishrambaug police later registered an FIR under sections 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt), 126(2) (wrongful restraint), 351(2) (criminal intimidation), 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace) and 353(2) (statements promoting enmity/hatred) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis , who also holds the home portfolio, strongly condemned the assault, saying every citizen had the right to express views. “Police have arrested the accused. In a city like Pune, such disputes should not turn violent. I have said earlier too that we should return Ganeshotsav celebrations to the traditional way. We may not achieve complete success in the first year, but we must make a sincere effort to reach that goal over time,” Fadnavis said.Deputy CM Eknath Shinde echoed the sentiment, saying the festival must be celebrated without causing inconvenience to residents. “Ganesh festival is an integral part of our tradition, and we must ensure that it is celebrated in a manner that preserves its essence. Nothing should be done that creates problems for local residents or causes inconvenience to people,” Shinde said.A video of the alleged attack that surfaced online showed Chavan challenging Bapat over his opposition to DJs and sound systems during Ganeshotsav and questioning his authority to speak on behalf of Pune residents. In the clip, Chavan is heard admitting to the assault, saying, “I assaulted him because he was speaking wrong.”Defending his action later, Chavan told reporters that Bapat was selectively targeting Ganeshotsav despite several other civic issues facing the city.Bapat, however, dismissed the attack as an attempt at “cheap publicity” and declared that it would not deter his campaign against noise pollution. “The attacker was like a zombie and there is no point arguing with such people. Police should do their job and take action against him. I know that what I am doing is right, so there is no question of stepping back,” he said.Pune police commissioner Amitesh Kumar confirmed that the accused had been detained and stressed that violence could not be justified under any circumstances. “Everyone has the freedom of speech. Violence is not justified,” Kumar said, adding that stringent action would follow.Kumar said Bapat had been provided round-the-clock police protection until further orders. Regarding a complaint filed against Bapat, Kumar said police were conducting an inquiry.Deputy police commissioner Krushikesh Rawale said Chavan has a criminal record, with at least two cases registered against him in 2014 and 2015. “Following the attack, we conducted a threat assessment and, based on the analysis, provided Bapat with security. One police security officer has been assigned to him, while guards have also been deployed outside his residence,” he said, adding that the security arrangement would be reviewed daily and a decision on its continuation would be taken accordingly.BJP corporator and PMC leader of the house Ganesh Bidkar said state govt had taken serious note of the incident. “BJP will ensure that Bapat is not harmed,” he said.The attack triggered widespread condemnation across party lines. Baramati MP Supriya Sule said ideological disagreements could never justify violence. “Responding to ideological differences with violence is a method that in no way benefits Maharashtra’s cultured and progressive tradition,” she said, stressing that everyone had the right to express an opinion in a democratic system.Union minister Murlidhar Mohol also denounced the assault, saying differences should be resolved through dialogue and debate, not physical attacks. “If we do not agree with someone’s position, it can be addressed through dialogue and by presenting an alternative viewpoint. Physical attack on a person for expressing his or her views is not the right way,” Mohol said.Congress state president Harshwardhan Sapkal, Congress member Prashant Jagtap and NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar joined the criticism. “If the price of ideological differences is beatings and arrests, then the coming times are truly going to be very tough,” Sapkal posted on X.Jagtap described the attack as an assault on Pune citizens who consistently raised concerns over loudspeakers and noise pollution.Following the incident, NCP (SP) workers, activists and citizens supporting Bapat staged a protest outside Vishrambaug police station. Bapat has emerged as a prominent voice in Pune’s ongoing debate over noise pollution during Ganeshotsav. He had earlier objected to the use of DJs and large sound systems at a Pune Municipal Corporation meeting, leading to a heated confrontation with representatives of Ganesh mandals and his eventual escort from the venue amid slogans and protests.Workers of Ganesh mandals condemned the attack on Bapat, saying such an attack was not acceptable.
Article Summary: Anti-noise campaigner Vidyanand Bapat of Narayan Peth was assaulted on Tilak Road in Pune. The accused, identified as Santosh Chavan, president of Kothrud- based Janjagruti Pratishthan, was taken into custody soon after the incident. The Vishrambaug police later registered an FIR under sections 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt) and 126 (wrongful restraint)

Article Title: Estonia minister quits after €70-million Ukraine shell deal involving Indian firm
Article Text:
Estonia minister quits in India-linked row

Estonia’s defence minister Hanno Pevkur has resigned over an arms deal to supply artillery shells to Ukraine using €70 million in European Union funds and involving Indian company, Euronews reported.It emerged on Wednesday that Estonia had paid the amount upfront for the shells, but the Indian company Neco Defence Munitions involved had no previous record of selling artillery ammunition.Estonian newspaper Eesti Ekspress reported that in 2024, Estonia signed a shell-supply deal with Italian-registered Datasel, owned by Indian company Neco Defence Munitions.Neither company had previously manufactured shells.The 2024 deal is now being challenged by Estonia in an arbitration case.Pevkur, who has been defence minister since 2022, said he was taking political responsibility for the controversy.“Although the minister does not count socks and ammunition or conduct contract negotiations, the National Audit Office’s criticisms, primarily concerning the activities of the Defence Forces and the Centre for Defence Investments, raise the question of political responsibility,” Pevkur said.The minister said he had not read the contracts, as defence ministers do not usually handle individual arms deals.“The defence minister does not conduct contract negotiations. The defence minister does not count socks and ammunition,” Pevkur said, adding: “The defence minister makes the fundamental decision to support Ukraine.”Pevkur’s resignation comes as the Russia-Ukraine war has already lasted longer than World War I, with no clear signs of peace or a return to normalcy.
Article Summary: Estonia’s defence minister Hanno Pevkur has resigned over an arms deal to supply artillery shells to Ukraine. The deal involved €70 million in European Union funds and involving Indian company. Indian company Neco Defence Munitions involved had no previous record of selling artillery ammunition.

Article Title: China’s grey-zone game: Why India must prepare for ‘armed coexistence’
Article Text:
India-China ties have thawed since the border skirmish in 2020.

Former foreign secretary

Vijay Gokhale

argues that China waits for a strategic opening, acts pre-emptively and then builds a narrative of self-defence.

His new book, “China’s Wars: The Politics and Diplomacy Behind its Military Coercion”, examines past conflicts and China’s recent grey-zone tactics.

In an interview with Indrajeet Rai, Gokhale explains why the

India-China relationship

has entered an era of “armed coexistence”, why a full-scale war is not the most likely outcome but cannot be ruled out, and how political uncertainty after Xi Jinping could produce global economic shocks or military adventurism.

You describe China as an opportunistic power. What does that mean, and when does Beijing decide to act pre-emptively?

China often depicts its own aggressive action as defensive and blames the other side. How central is this narrative warfare to its strategy?

China’s grey-zone strategy seeks to steadily pressure and exhaust rivals while avoiding the escalation of tensions into full-scale war.

You argue that China is pursuing sustained grey-zone coercion. How does this work against India?

Does that mean a large-scale India-China war is unlikely in the foreseeable future?

China’s capabilities against Taiwan have grown, while the US is distracted by several conflicts. Could Xi Jinping move on Taiwan to secure his legacy?

Xi has removed the age and term limits that helped institutionalise succession. What happens after him and why should India worry?

China has few formal allies and did little visibly to support Iran. Does it lack the partnerships needed to become a global leader?

Edited excerpts:By opportunistic power, I did not intend to suggest that China is very different from other major powers. In the case studies in my book, China waited for the international situation to turn favourable, or for some advantage to accrue from its relations with other major powers, before carrying out conflict with a neighbour or another country. It used opportunity strategically to achieve its goals.The Chinese idea of preventive deterrence or preventive conflict differs from the Western concept. In the West, deterrence is a counteraction intended to stop the adversary from escalating. In the Chinese context, it is pre-emptive: China acts even before the adversary has had the chance to act first. The aim is to deliver a political and psychological shock so the adversary desists or fears retaliation.The 1962 conflict is one example. There was no indication that India intended to launch a military assault. But China used the words of then PM Jawaharlal Nehru and an international situation dominated by the Cuban missile crisis to act pre-emptively against India.The Chinese Communist Party utilised China’s difficult circumstances after the collapse of the empire and projected itself as the only organisation capable of pulling the country out of its problems. It placed the blame for China’s declining economy and global influence on external circumstances. It played the victim’s card: China was perennially the victim, and the party was the instrument that would restore it as a major power.The blame, therefore, was always placed on somebody else: The colonial powers, the United States in the Korean War, India in the 1962 war and the Soviet Union in the 1969 conflict. There was never an acknowledgement that some responsibility also fell on China.This is not limited to foreign policy. The party does not take responsibility for major domestic failures either: The Great Leap Forward, the Cultural Revolution or the 1989 Tiananmen incident. Blame falls on an external force or a few bad elements, never the party itself.Since 1979, China has not fought a real conflict. The leadership made economic development the priority, and successive leaders after Mao Zedong focused on reform and opening up.But China was not willing to give up the use of force; it changed the manner in which force was used. Instead of hot wars or major conflict, it engaged and continues to engage in very low-intensity military conflict, popularly known as grey-zone warfare.Grey-zone warfare uses threats or actual force while staying below the threshold that might tempt the rival to launch a counteroffensive. It punishes or deters, but stops short of making the rival feel compelled to push back with force. We see it along the Line of Actual Control, in the South China Sea and in the East China Sea.I have characterised the situation on the LAC after 2020 as the end of peaceful coexistence and the beginning of armed coexistence. Armed coexistence does not mean conflict. It means China will continue to take grey-zone military action around the LAC to keep us tied down and to exhaust us not only financially - because keeping forces and equipment at those heights costs a lot - but also in terms of men and material.This fulfils a key Chinese objective: Keeping India confined to South Asia.Apart from the United States, there are few potential rivals in this century, and India is one. If you look at India, it's geographical location, its population size, its territorial size, its talent, it's economic potential. All of it lends a credence to the belief that India can become a major power in this century. And clearly, China would like to delay that possibility.Nobody can predict this definitively. China and its decision-making processes are opaque, and there are no alternative channels of information such as free media or civil society.China is a mature state focused on becoming the strongest economy and power in the world. On a rational cost-benefit analysis, the price of a major war with India could exceed the benefits. Logically, China would be reluctant to engage in such a conflict.At the end of the day, however, it is impossible to predict. We have to be prepared for the worst, while logically understanding that a hot conflict with India may not be in China’s interest in the foreseeable future.An American commander of the Indo-Pacific Command, Admiral Philip Davidson, suggested that by 2027 China would have the military capability to launch an assault on Taiwan. Some interpreted that to mean China would attack by 2027, but he did not actually say this.China’s capabilities for an assault on an island have substantially increased: Landing craft, area-denial capabilities, communication systems and anti-ship missiles.It is one thing for a major power to bomb another country and destroy its infrastructure, and quite another to occupy or conquer it. That requires a very large commitment of forces and material, with no assured guarantee of victory.China’s demographic decline is already causing anxiety. An assault would mean mass casualties because boots on the ground would be required. After Galwan, India acknowledged within days that 20 soldiers had been martyred; China took much longer to admit fatalities. With Taiwan potentially producing casualties in the hundreds or thousands, Beijing will worry about the domestic impact.This is where democracy, for all its weaknesses, becomes a strength. A democratic government has electoral and constitutional legitimacy to act, including in war. In China, the party claims it has popular support but has never tested that proposition. The reaction to large-scale war casualties is unpredictable.Deng Xiaoping introduced two reforms that stabilised succession: Those above 68 could not continue in top party positions, and the president was limited to two five-year terms. This helped ensure smooth transitions from Jiang Zemin to Hu Jintao and then to Xi Jinping.Xi has abolished the age and term limits. In an authoritarian system, no leader will voluntarily give up power because enemies may find it easier to target him, and he cannot be certain a successor will not misuse authority against him.China could enter a period of political uncertainty and potentially turmoil as Xi ages and factions emerge in a contest for power. It is unclear whether this happens before or after his death, or whether he intends to stand for a fourth term.Because China is the world’s second-largest economy, domestic turmoil would affect its economy, military and diplomacy and create huge ripple effects abroad. Beleaguered regimes also sometimes use an external threat to divert attention. India must consider whether turmoil could produce military adventurism and how to preserve its national interests, sovereignty and territorial integrity.China lacks the United States’ large network of treaty allies. But we should not underestimate the goodwill it enjoys. The Belt and Road Initiative has been welcomed as an alternative route to development. Western assistance often came with harsh conditions; China offers fewer and less onerous strings. Nobody gives aid for free, but China has built substantial diplomatic influence.There was little need for China to do more in the Iran war. It could neither persuade the United States to stop nor force peace. It protected its oil interests and relations with Iran and the Gulf countries without entering the mediation game.When the conflict ends, Iran will rebuild using its oil and gas wealth. It is unlikely to trust the West, while China can build infrastructure at a scale few others can match. China needs energy; Iran needs infrastructure and money. That creates an enormous downstream economic opportunity and a win-win situation. Why would China get significantly involved now when there seems to be no clear way out of the conflict?India should not look at the world order through an either-or lens. The United States and China will both remain major powers. The question is how, in a triangular or quadrangular relationship, including the European Union if it acts as a union, we create an international framework relevant to this century.India has objective advantages: Its location, demographics and consumer base; tested political stability; an independent military capability and growing defence industry; and talent.I do not see how India can fail to become a major power in this century. The international order is disintegrating and all states are hedging their bets; India is doing so too. The task is not to choose a US-led or China-led order. It is to help build an order in which India is one of the leaders.
Article Summary: Vijay Gokhale argues that China waits for a strategic opening, acts pre- emptively and then builds a narrative of self-defence. His new book, “China’s Wars: The Politics and Diplomacy Behind its Military Coercion’, examines past conflicts and China‘s recent grey-zone tactics.

Article Title: Chirag Paswan vs Jitan Manjhi in Bihar: SC 'creamy layer' debate divides NDA; will it open up a Pandora's box?
Article Text:
Chirag vs Manjhi: SC ‘creamy layer’ debate puts Bihar NDA unity to test.

Turf war for Dalit leadership in Bihar

Manjhi has accused Chirag Paswan of seeking to maintain 'Dusadh dominance'.

Homogeneous group vs categorisation

Chirag Paswan demanded resignation of Manjhi and his son Santosh Kumar Suman.

Two-fold challenge

'BJP testing people's mood'

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you support economic criteria over caste-based reservations? Yes, it should be prioritised for fairness. No, caste discrimination needs to be addressed first. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Could the open sparring over “quota within quota” between two prominent Dalit faces of Bihar last month open up a Pandora’s box for the BJP-led NDA government? Union ministers Jitan Ram Manjhi and Chirag Paswan engaged in an open war of words last week over a separate sub-category for the most deprived Dalit sections.Manjhi hails from the Musahar community and wants a sub-quota for the marginalised SC communities. Manjhi’s son Santosh Kumar Suman, who is the Bihar minor water resources minister, has demanded a review of the country’s reservation policy to assess which sections have benefited and which have remained deprived even after 79 years of independence. The father-son duo claims they are not against reservations but want either an increase in quota or separate arrangements for sections still deprived of its benefits after seven decades.Chirag Paswan, son of Late Ram Vilas Paswan, objected to calls to introduce the “creamy layer” provision in SC/ST reservations and insisted that those advocating such a move should first resign from their positions. He stressed that the reservation policy was not based on economic status but was designed to address centuries of social discrimination, exclusion and untouchability.This is not the first time the two leaders have openly engaged in a war of words on issues.There have been instances in the past when the two Dalit leaders have openly taken diametrically opposite stands. The latest point of friction was the Bharat Tiwari encounter case of Bhojpur district. While Chirag Paswan vowed to prevail upon Bihar's BJP-led government to ensure that punishment was meted out to all police officials involved in his encounter, Manjhi asserted that police were justified in having opened fire on the 28-year-old man with an "unlicensed" weapon. Tiwari, a self-styled social and political activist, was shot dead following a heated exchange on June 17 when officials of the local administration and police visited his place to interrogate him in connection with incendiary social media posts.Political observers feel the open friction between the two leaders is more of a political fight for Dalit leadership in the state. Analyst Naval Kishore Choudhary, who has observed Bihar politics for decades, says Manjhi and Paswan are engaged in a turf war."The two leaders represent two different constituencies within the SC community and are in race to establish themselves as a bigger leader within the NDA in Bihar. By taking contradictory stands, they are catering to their own constituencies within the community. There perhaps is a tussle between them to prove who is more important for NDA in Bihar," Choudhary said.However, the current issue of their discord, “quota within quota”, is not just contentious but also politically sensitive. The BJP has strategically avoided a debate on the issue of sub-quota within the Dalits, perhaps realising the uncertain fallout of any such debate.A Supreme Court judgment in August 2024, in a 6:1 majority ruling, had allowed states to sub-categorise castes within the Scheduled Castes (SC) based on socio-economic backwardness and degree of under-representation in govt jobs to ensure that the larger pie of 15% SC quota goes to the backwards among them.It had also asked governments to devise suitable criteria to bar the ‘creamy layer’ among SCs and STs from availing reservation. In the process, the SC overruled an earlier judgment of a five-judge bench in EV Chinnaiah case, which had said the SCs were a homogeneous group and could not be sub-categorised.The Modi government had in 2017 constituted a four-member Commission headed by Justice (Retd.) G. Rohini in October 2017 to examine the extent of inequitable distribution of benefits of reservation among the OBCs and to work out the mechanism, criteria, norms and parameters in a scientific approach for sub-categorisation within them. The Commission submitted its report to President Droupadi Murmu on July 21, 2023. However, the report has not been made public yet.Clearly, the government perhaps wants to avoid opening a Pandora’s box. More so at a time when it faces a competing challenge from the upper caste communities also. There were protests against reservations in the national capital last month, and the government engaged with the protesters. On August 21, several people held a protest in the national capital following a call by Reservation Hatao Andolan (Scrap Reservation), an Instagram-based page. The protesters are demanding the scrapping of quotas, saying that economic criteria should be given precedence over caste in determining eligibility for government support and reservation.Later, the representatives of the group held a meeting with Union minister J P Nadda and engaged in a "cordial discussion". "Following the movement that took place at Jantar Mantar on 21 August, cordial discussions were held, as per the pre-determined schedule, with Harsh Dubey, Ran Bahadur Singh Chauhan, and Mrityunjay Pathak, members of the team. In this connection, we will meet again soon," Nadda said in a post on X after the meeting.Nadda's meeting with Reservation Hatao Andolan representatives drew questions from opponents. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke asked Nadda to explain the Modi government's stand on the anti-reservation movement and questioned what Prime Minister Narendra Modi has to say about the August 21 protest. AAP Delhi unit president Saurabh Bharadwaj also sought clarity from Nadda on the government's position, referring to the demand for reconsideration of reservations.These political attacks notwithstanding, the BJP has to keep in mind the upper-caste sentiments. The upper caste vote has largely been with the BJP barring some exceptions, but ahead of the crucial assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh there are reports of discontent in the community.For the BJP, the challenge is two-fold. On the one hand, it has to keep the anti-reservation protesters engaged without enraging the pro-reservation groups. On the other, it has to strike a balance between competing demands of allies on sub-categorisation within the SC community.The BJP already faces pressure from the marginalised groups after stay on University Grants Commission (UGC) rules calling out caste discrimination in universities. The saffron party is also battling opposition allegations that the 2027 caste census deliberately obscures caste data. The 40 questions which are part of the census ask for many personal details, which have not so far been required for any census. However, it does not have a drop-down box for caste, nor does it ask people to self-identify as OBC to allow for proper collation of caste data.Political analyst Uday Chandra says internal conflicts within the SC community is a reality. This is more so in Bihar where Dalit identity is not totally consolidated like in other states. “The “Jati” name takes precedence over the Dalit identity in Bihar and that explains why there is a competing interest between the two Dalit leaders in the state,” Uday Chandra says.“The BJP also faces the challenge of forming new social coalitions in the runup to 2029 Lok Sabha elections. The 2014 and 2019 social coalitions which helped the BJP electorally are starting to fray and may not be effective for electoral gains,” he adds.That perhaps explains why the BJP is treading cautiously and may not be averse to the idea of “quota within quota” like it exits within the OBCs. Nitish Kumar formed the group of EBCs in Bihar and they powered his politics for years.The BJP may also ponder at the prospect of making electoral gains by prioritising the deprived within the Dalits. No wonder, the opposition parties in Bihar are already accusing the BJP of using the two ministers to test people’s mood on the issue.Bihar's leader of the opposition Tejashwi Yadav said: "The BJP is doing all this drama from behind. They are testing people's mood, putting pebbles in the water and seeing what happens." Referring to Majhi and Paswan, he said: "These people are merely characters. They only want posts. They are greedy for positions, chairs, bungalows and security, but have left society behind."Congress MP Pramod Tiwari said Union ministers making allegations against each other "goes against the Constitution". "Perhaps they do not realise that the principle of collective responsibility applies to the Council of Ministers. Whatever a minister says remains the government's position until it is contradicted," he said.But the BJP may not want to make any new experiment now as the very idea is fraught with huge political risks. Hence, to put the sparring Dalit leaders on the back foot, Bihar minister and senior BJP leader Lakhendra Paswan posed a pointed question to both the Union ministers.Without directly endorsing either position, he asked how many people from their respective communities, beyond their immediate families, they had actually helped advance. He reiterated what he described as the BJP’s position on reservation, declaring, “If there is BJP, there is reservation.” BJP national spokesperson Dr Guru Prakash Paswan also reiterated that the government has a clear stand regarding the reservation issue. "Reservation will exist till discrimination exists in society, and our government has strengthened this system. Whatever one says on this can be their personal opinion, but for social justice, the BJP is committed to fulfilling the vows of B.R. Ambedkar," he said.So, while the BJP watches its two allies in Bihar fight, it would hope that the issue does not snowball into a controversy that goes out of hand.
Article Summary: Jitan Ram Manjhi and Chirag Paswan engaged in an open war of words last week over a separate sub-category for the most deprived Dalit sections. Political observers feel the open friction between the two leaders is more of a political fight for Dalit leadership in the state.

Article Title: Ladakh to have seven hill councils now, elections for new LAHDCs soon

SRINAGAR: All seven districts of Ladakh will now have autonomous hill development councils, with lieutenant governor Vinai Kumar Saxena approving a notification to this effect Thursday. The move paves the way for local self-governance in all seven districts of the UT through the councils, elections to which will be held soon.So far, only Leh and Kargil districts had Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Councils (LAHDCs). On July 13, the central govt announced the creation of LAHDCs for Sham, Nubra, Changthang, Zanskar and Drass districts, too. The UT administration had notified the creation of the five new districts in April this year.“The framework of elected local self-governance, which was limited to Leh and Kargil, will thereby be also extended to the five newly created districts in the UT,” a govt spokesperson said.The elections to the newly constituted councils will be held in due course after a formal notification is issued under section 8 of the LAHDC Act, 1997, the spokesperson said, adding that the notification would come into force from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.The LAHDC-Leh was established under the LAHDC Act, 1995, while the LAHDC-Kargil was set up in 2003. Elections for both the councils are held every five years.Currently, only the LAHDC-Kargil has an elected body, as elections to its counterpart in Leh could not be held following the Sept 24 violence last year, when four people were killed after the police allegedly opened fire on protesters demanding Sixth Schedule protections and statehood for the region.In a statement here, Saxena thanked PM Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah for the historic step, stating that the establishment of the seven councils was a milestone in strengthening grassroots governance in Ladakh, allowing local aspirations and priorities to be reflected more effectively in district-level planning and development.
Article Summary: The move paves the way for local self-governance in all seven districts of the UT through the councils. On July 13, the central govt announced the creation of LAHDCs for Sham, Nubra, Changthang, Zanskar and Drass districts, too.

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Thursday accused Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann , his wife Gurpreet Kaur and AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal of allegedly running a corruption and extortion "syndicate" through intermediaries to settle rape cases in the state in exchange for bribes of up to Rs 5 crore.The allegations were levelled by BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari, who played purported audio recordings and cited other material at a press conference in New Delhi. The BJP described the alleged arrangement as the Aam Aadmi Party's "loot model".The allegations come against the backdrop of a National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) inquiry into a complaint alleging that Gurpreet Kaur demanded Rs 5 crore to quash a rape case. On August 21, the NHRC directed the Punjab chief secretary and director general of police to inquire into the allegations and submit an Action Taken Report within two weeks.There was no immediate response from the Aam Aadmi Party to the allegations. However, AAP's Punjab unit has rejected the charges, with AAP state Women's Wing president and MLA Amandeep Kaur Arora calling them "baseless".Addressing reporters, Bhandari alleged that Mann and his wife had used intermediaries across Punjab to broker deals involving criminal cases."The audio recordings that we are going to play before you, and the evidence that has come before us, point towards the fact that Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann is running a new loot racket and a new corruption racket," Bhandari said."In this corruption racket, allegations are that he and his wife, through middlemen, are seeking bribes of up to Rs 5 crore to get legitimate rape cases settled," he alleged.Bhandari claimed that intermediaries had been deployed across the state on the instructions of Mann and his wife to facilitate the alleged transactions."The chief minister and the wife of the chief minister have deputed middlemen across Punjab. These middlemen, on the instructions of the chief minister and his wife, have innovated a new model of corruption, which we call the Aam Aadmi Party's 'loot model', in which these middlemen are taking bribes of Rs 5 crore to settle rape cases," he further alleged.He also sought to link Kejriwal to the alleged arrangement, referring to him as Punjab's "super CM"."The middleman is speaking to a relative of the accused and saying that we have also informed 'CM sahab' about this and now CM sahab has also become involved," he alleged.Bhandari questioned whether the chief minister, his wife and Kejriwal were involved in what he described as a broader corruption network."Does the chief minister and his wife run a syndicate in which they are taking bribes and money to withdraw rape cases?" he said."Has the chief minister's office become a syndicate of corruption?" Bhandari asked. "Has the Aam Aadmi Party's 'loot model' now become a model in Punjab where money is being taken for rape cases, just like the corruption and loot model of the 'Sheesh Mahal' in Delhi?" he asked.Bhandari also cited the NHRC's intervention, saying the commission had already sought a report from Punjab authorities."On August 21, 2026, the national human rights commission, taking cognisance of this matter, has already written a letter to the chief secretary of the Punjab government and the Punjab DGP.""It has asked to investigate whether the chief minister's office and the chief minister himself are running a corruption racket in Punjab in which bribes of Rs 5 crore are being offered to withdraw cases of rape victims," Bhandari said.The controversy has also prompted the Shiromani Akali Dal to seek a separate probe. A high-level SAD delegation led by party president Sukhbir Singh Badal met Punjab Governor Gulab Singh Kataria in Chandigarh on Thursday and demanded a CBI inquiry into alleged corruption in the Chief Minister's Office and alleged attempts to protect a rape accused.The delegation submitted a 300-page dossier along with other documents and evidence to the Governor in support of its allegations.The SAD demand followed the NHRC notice issued last month in connection with allegations that Rs 5 crore was demanded and accepted to shield an accused in a rape case.Addressing reporters after meeting the Governor, Badal alleged that the state government was attempting to protect a rape accused."On one side is the rapist and those protecting him, and on the other side are those helpless girls. I want to see which side the media takes. If you do not show our press conference or highlight this issue, it means you are under pressure of the Punjab government and supporting the rapist. I hope the media will stand with those helpless girls," Badal said.The allegations and counter-allegations come as the NHRC inquiry into the complaint remains underway, with Punjab authorities required to submit an Action Taken Report to the commission.

Article Title: Manipur violence: 306 killed, 49 missing since May 2023

Violence erupted over ST status demand

At least 306 people have been killed and 49 remain missing in the ethnic violence that broke out in Manipur in May 2023, state home minister Govindas Konthoujam told the Assembly on Thursday.Responding to a query by BJP MLA Sapam Ranjan Singh on the second day of the ongoing Assembly session, Konthoujam said the figures were recorded as of August 31, 2026.“Since the violence started on May 3, 2023, 306 people have died, and 49 people are still missing as of August 31, 2026,” he said.The ethnic clashes between the Meitei and Kuki-Zo communities began on May 3, 2023, after a ‘Tribal Solidarity March’ was organised in the hill districts to protest the Meitei community’s demand for Scheduled Tribe status.Meiteis account for around 53 per cent of Manipur’s population and live mainly in the Imphal Valley, while tribals, including Nagas and Kukis, constitute around 40 per cent and reside predominantly in the hill districts.The prolonged violence resulted in widespread displacement and triggered significant political developments in the state.President’s Rule was imposed in Manipur on February 13, 2025, after then chief minister N Biren Singh resigned amid the prolonged ethnic conflict. The 60-member Assembly was subsequently placed under suspended animation.President’s Rule was revoked on February 4, 2026, paving the way for the formation of a new government under BJP leader Yumnam Khemchand Singh as chief minister.
Article Summary: Violence erupted over the Meitei community’s demand for Scheduled Tribe status. The prolonged violence resulted in widespread displacement and triggered significant political developments in the state. At least 306 people have been killed and 49 remain missing in the ethnic violence that broke out in May 2023.

Article Title: Nalsar row: SC strikes down BCI orders, says it has 'no statutory power to regulate conduct of students'
Article Text:
How the NALSAR row began

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you support the decision to set aside the BCI authority over law students? Yes, I support the decision. No, I believe BCI should regulate them. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday held that the Bar Council of India has "no statutory authority to regulate the conduct of law students". The court set aside two BCI notifications issued against students of Hyderabad's Nalsar University of Law.A bench comprising CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana passed the order.The orders were linked to the students' protest over Chief Justice of India Surya Kant's proposed participation in the university's convocation.The court's observation came after the BCI initially directed state Bar Councils not to enrol Nalsar's 2026 law graduates as advocates following a student campaign opposing CJI Surya Kant's proposed participation as chief guest at the university's convocation.Also read - BCI action, U-turn and SC rebuke: How NALSAR students' protest against CJI kicked up a row The BCI later withdrew the directive and allowed the graduates to be enrolled while an inquiry was pending.The controversy began after several Nalsar students submitted representations asking the university to reconsider its invitation to CJI Surya Kant. The students referred to remarks attributed to the CJI during a hearing concerning alleged police excesses against protesters during a July 20 march to Parliament.At least six representations were submitted by students from different batches, with the first being sent on July 23. The students argued that inviting the CJI was inconsistent with the university's stated commitment to constitutional rights, access to justice and reasoned engagement with grievances.One representation cited the CJI's response to an offer to show videos of the alleged police action: "We are not interested in videos; we don’t have time to watch." It also quoted him as telling counsel: "Don’t waste our time, and don’t waste your time".The students maintained that their objection was rooted in constitutional values and not disrespect towards the judicial office."We respect the CJI’s position. But we have been taught the Constitution and constitutional values, and we don’t want to support something that goes against those values," a student who was also part of the Student bar council had told TOI.The dispute escalated when BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra directed state Bar Councils not to enrol Nalsar's 2026 law graduates as advocates until further orders.The BCI sought a report from Nalsar identifying students who had allegedly initiated, organised or mobilised the campaign against CJI Surya Kant's participation in the convocation.The council's initial communication stated, “Till further orders, no student of Nalsar University of Law, who has obtained law degree in the year 2026, shall be enrolled by any state bar council as an advocate.”It also said, “A student of Law, having no regard or respect for the highest judicial office of the country, is not expected to be a responsible or sensible advocate, teacher or a judge. Such persons shall always be a liability on the profession. Such conduct reflects adversely upon the person’s suitability for entry into or association with the legal profession and is inconsistent with the dignity, discipline and ethical standards of the legal profession. ”The BCI further alleged that some members of Nalsar's academic staff had been involved in "misleading, instigating and misguiding" students.“As per some reliable sources, there exists groupism and dirty politics among some of the academic staff and they have played a very active role in misleading, instigating and misguiding the students. This is a very serious matter. The teachers, instead of involving themselves in their teaching job, are doing nasty politics in the campus. BCI, being the regulator of Legal Education cannot be a mute spectator of such a serious situation. ”The directive drew criticism from sections of the legal fraternity, with Supreme Court bar association president Vikas Singh describing the move as arbitrary, illegal and disproportionate, while maintaining that he did not support the students' opposition to the CJI's invitation.The BCI withdrew its original directive within hours amid the criticism. In its revised communication, Mishra said the council had “thoroughly discussed and deliberated” on the earlier letter and modified its direction.He said the “vast majority” of Nalsar's 2026 graduating students were innocent and “were not inclined to take part in the move of disrespect”. However, he added, “It has been further reported by some reliable sources that a handful of teachers and outsiders were instrumental in instigating innocent students.”The revised decision permitted the 2026 graduates to be enrolled while the BCI awaited an inquiry report from Nalsar.
Article Summary: The court set aside two BCI notifications issued against students of Hyderabad's Nalsar University of Law. The orders were linked to the students' protest over Chief Justice of India Surya Kant's proposed participation in the university's convocation. The BCI initially directed state Bar Councils not to enrol NALSar's 2026 law graduates as advocates.

Article Title: TMC alleges 'systematic misuse of police' by BJP in Bengal; writes to President Murmu
Article Text:
TMC MP Derek O'Brien

NEW DELHI: The Trinamool Congress TMC ) on Thursday wrote to President Droupadi Murmu and West Bengal governor RN Ravi, seeking time for party delegations to meet them and highlight the alleged lawlessness in the state.The TMC accused the ruling BJP of “systematically misusing” the West Bengal Police, calling it “disturbing.”"TMC workers are being targeted by the police across the state. Party offices are being vandalised. The police are following no rules. Police are acting openly as BJP cadres. There is utter lawlessness here. In this situation, we have written to the President of India, and the Trinamool Congress has written to the Governor of West Bengal, seeking an urgent appointment of a Trinamool Congress delegation to discuss the disturbing situation in Bengal," the party's Rajya Sabha MP Derek O'Brien told reporters.The development came hours after TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee alleged that "BJP hooligans armed with weapons" stormed the party's Camac Street office in Kolkata in the early hours of the day and vandalised the premises, assaulted staff, and damaged electronic equipment."What happened at Camac Street this morning is a disgraceful assault on the rule of law. At around 4.30 am, BJP hooligans, armed with weapons, stormed our party office in the heart of Kolkata.They attacked our people, snatched their phones, smashed furniture, ransacked the premises and destroyed electronic equipment. And where was Kolkata Police? For nearly TWO HOURS, despite repeated calls and emails from our people and lawyers, there was no response. This is outrageous and unacceptable. We demand the immediate arrest of every person involved in this attack," he wrote on X.The Diamond Harbour MP, nephew of TMC supremo and former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee, asked chief minister Suvendu Adhikari if he was “scared” of the TMC and was therefore resorting to "intimidation."“This is what the BJP has done to my party office in the early hours of this morning. Will the Governor of WB act? Will the Union Home Minister act? Will the PMO act? Or will they continue to look the other way? It is high time the judiciary, particularly the Calcutta High Court, takes serious note of what is happening and acts to uphold the rule of law in West Bengal. And one simple question for Suvendu Adhikari: why are you so scared of the Trinamool Congress and of me that you have to resort to this kind of intimidation? If this is how the Opposition is to be treated in West Bengal, through violence, vandalism and intimidation, then the Chief Minister has no moral authority to remain in office.He must resign. This is not democracy. This is political thuggery... Nothing will be forgotten,” Abhishek Banerjee added.The BJP, meanwhile, rejected Abhishek Banerjee’s allegation of “vendetta”, arguing that if that were the case, no TMC leader would have remained “unscathed” after the party’s defeat in the April assembly elections, which ended its 15-year rule in West Bengal."If the BJP were engaging in vendetta politics, then after the election results were declared, none of the defeated Trinamool Congress MLAs, ministers, and MPs would have remained unscathed... Trinamool members are throwing eggs at each other and vandalising each other's offices. Those who faced injustice at the hands of Abhishek Banerjee, when he was a top party leader, understand the situation," BJP state president Samik Bhattacharya said.
Article Summary: The Trinamool Congress TMC ) on Thursday wrote to President Droupadi Murmu and West Bengal governor RN Ravi. The development came hours after TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee alleged that "BJP hooligans armed with weapons" stormed the party's Camac Street office in Kolkata in the early hours of the day.

Article Title: CJP's Ashutosh Ranka meets Akhilesh Yadav ahead of UP polls, sparks buzz
Article Text:
CJP’s student campaign

Meeting ahead of UP polls





LUCKNOW: CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka met Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav in Lucknow ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, according to news agency PTI.Accroding to SP chief spokesperson Rajendra Chaudhary said, Ashutosh Ranka and SP chief Akhilesh Yadav met in the Lucknow on Thursday evening. He said he was not aware of the details of their discussion.The meeting is believed to have touched on issues affecting young people, including unemployment and school education. Yadav has frequently criticised the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh over these issues.According to sources, the two held a closed-door meeting for around 90 minutes from about 4pm at the office of the Janeshwar Mishra Trust, located near the SP headquarters.Ranka left the premises after the meeting without speaking to the media. The SP chief Akilesh Yadav also did not issue any statement on the purpose or outcome of the meeting.Sources said the discussion may have included concerns of students, as well as those of Gen Z and Gen Alpha. Education-related issues may also have been discussed, although there was no official confirmation of the details.The meeting comes amid the CJP’s recent activities over student-related issues.Yadav had earlier raised concerns after Ranka was allegedly attacked in Rajasthan last month while taking part in the CJP’s “School Thik Karo” campaign.SP leaders have also shown support for student protests. After police used a lathi charge during the CJP’s agitation at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, party MP Dimple Yadav and Azamgarh MP Dharmendra Yadav visited the protest site and expressed solidarity with the students.Akhilesh Yadav has also spoken in support of the student movement led by the CJP on several occasions.The meeting comes at a significant time, with Uttar Pradesh scheduled to hold Assembly elections early next year.The SP has been targeting the BJP-led state government over issues such as unemployment, education and inflation.Yadav, a former Uttar Pradesh chief minister, has repeatedly raised concerns over school closures. He has questioned the Centre over the issue at the national level and criticised the Uttar Pradesh government over the closure of primary schools in the state.
Article Summary: CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka met Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav in Lucknow. The meeting is believed to have touched on issues affecting young people, including unemployment and school education. Yadav has frequently criticised the BJP government in Uttar Pradesh over these issues.

Article Title: Blinkit's Mangaluru storage sealed after customer finds worm inside egg
Article Text:
Food safety officials inspected a Blinkit facility in Mangaluru after a consumer found a worm in an egg





MANGALURU: Food safety officials in Karnataka inspected a Blinkit online retail facility in Mangaluru after a consumer alleged that a worm was found inside an egg purchased through the quick-commerce platform.The complaint was reportedly submitted to Health Minister U T Khader, following which officials inspected the facility operating from Falnir Square in the city's Falnir area.During the inspection, officials found packets containing broken eggs and directed the facility staff to immediately remove and dispose of the affected stock, according to an official release.As a precautionary measure, the storage room was temporarily closed and sealed to allow thorough cleaning and sanitisation of the food storage area.The Food Safety Department said it would issue a notice to the establishment seeking an explanation over the incident. Further action will be decided based on the inspection findings and the response submitted by the facility management.The inspection comes amid increased scrutiny of food safety and hygiene standards in Karnataka. In a separate action, the Department of Food Safety and Drug Administration recently closed and seized a kitchen at Chairman's Club in Sahakaranagar's Dollars Colony area of Bengaluru after officials found multiple alleged violations during a special inspection drive conducted on September 3.Officials said around 40 kg of expired chilli was found and seized during the inspection. The department also flagged improper labelling of certain food products, unhygienic conditions in food preparation and storage areas, alleged use or storage of unauthorised artificial colours, lapses in food handling and storage practices, and the storage of vegetarian and non-vegetarian food products together.The department said it would continue inspections and take legal action against food businesses found violating food safety and hygiene norms.
Article Summary: Food safety officials in Karnataka inspected a Blinkit facility in Mangaluru. A consumer alleged that a worm was found inside an egg purchased through the quick-commerce platform. The complaint was reportedly submitted to Health Minister U T Khader. During the inspection, officials found packets containing broken eggs.

Article Title: Nepal flash floods: Relatives hold symbolic funerals for thousands missing as toll crosses 1,243
Article Text:
The death toll from devastating flash floods in the Nepal-Tibet region rose to 1,243 on Thursday.

The death toll from devastating flash floods in the Nepal-Tibet region rose to 1,243 on Thursday, as rescue teams battled heavy rain and thick debris while searching for people believed to be trapped in tunnels and underground power facilities along the Bhotekoshi River.Prime Minister Balendra Shah said Nepal must raise the disaster’s connection to climate change with the international community, as families held symbolic funerals for relatives who remain missing following last week’s floods.Speaking at the fifth daily press briefing in Kathmandu, ministry of foreign affairs spokesperson Lok Bahadur Chhetri said authorities had begun conducting temporary burials for victims as search and rescue operations continued around the clock.Chhetri said 11,993 people had been rescued, while 1,114 bodies had been recovered. Around 3,900 people remain unaccounted for, he said, urging relatives of those missing to provide DNA samples at the Nepal Police Hospital in Maharajgunj or their nearest District Police Office to help forensic teams with identification.He also outlined international assistance being provided to Nepal. A 19-member forensic team from India is working with Nepal Police on DNA analysis, while specialised teams and equipment have also arrived from China, Singapore and South Korea to support identification and recovery efforts.Rescue teams from the Nepali Army, Nepal Police and Armed Police Force are working with international specialists from India, China and South Korea to clear mud, debris and boulders from underground hydropower facilities in areas including Langtang, Chilime and Upper Trisuli.According to the ANI report, more than 300 foreign nationals have been safely rescued, while around 590 citizens from 34 countries remain unaccounted for.Working with Chinese authorities, Nepal has also helped evacuate about 2,500 pilgrims returning from Mount Kailash through the Hilsa and Tatopani border crossings and via air routes through Lhasa. Efforts are also underway to clear stranded cargo and assist Nepali nationals near the Kerung border.Addressing Parliament earlier Wednesday, Prime Minister Balendra Shah said the catastrophic August 26 Bhotekoshi River floods, triggered by a high-altitude Himalayan avalanche, underscored the growing threat posed by climate change across the region.Shah said nearly 4,000 people remain missing across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading, stressing that addressing the effects of climate change requires a collective global effort.As Nepal continues to coordinate international assistance from India, China, the United States, Japan, the Asian Development Bank, the World Bank, the European Union and the United Nations, authorities are deploying available resources toward emergency relief, searches for missing people and long-term recovery.According to Nepal Police, 348 bodies were recovered in Chitwan, 217 in Nawalparasi East, 190 in Nawalparasi West and 155 in Nuwakot. Another 66 bodies were recovered in Gorkha, 59 in Dhading, 45 in Rasuwa and 38 in Tanahu.A total of 7,912 police personnel have been deployed to flood-hit areas to assist with search and rescue operations, distribute relief supplies and manage recovered bodies.Authorities have also published details of 911 unidentified bodies on the Nepal Police website to help families identify missing relatives.Meanwhile, rainwater accumulating inside a hydropower tunnel has created additional difficulties for search and rescue teams working in areas affected by the Bhotekoshi floods, said Dharma Raj Uprety, executive chief of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA).Search operations have been particularly challenging because of the hazardous conditions inside the project’s tunnels. Teams from the Nepali Army and Armed Police Force, along with foreign technical experts and project employees, are continuing efforts to locate workers who remain missing.As per the PTI report, Ganesh Karki, former president of the Independent Power Producers’ Association, Nepal (IPPAN), said rescue operations have also been slowed by difficulties transporting heavy equipment to the tunnels.
Article Summary: The death toll from devastating flash floods in the Nepal-Tibet region rose to 1,243 on Thursday. Rescue teams battled heavy rain and thick debris while searching for people believed to be trapped in tunnels and underground power facilities. Prime Minister Balendra Shah said Nepal must raise the disaster’s connection to climate change with the international community.

Article Title: Cars of Maharashtra ex-minister Dilip Kamble vandalised outside his residence
Article Text:
In photo: One of the damaged vehicles





PUNE: Two cars belonging to former minister of state and BJP leader Dilip Kamble were vandalised by unidentified persons outside his residence in Ghorpadi late Wednesday night. The incident took place at a housing society on BT Kawade Road.According to police, Kamble had gone out with his family on Wednesday evening. Between 8pm and 9pm, unidentified persons allegedly attacked the two cars parked outside his house with stones and bamboo sticks.Kamble said the vandalism appeared to be a deliberate and pre-planned attempt to target him. He also expressed concern over the cutting of CCTV wires at his residence.“We had gone out around 8pm and returned around 9pm, only to find that our vehicles had been vandalised. I feel this was a deliberate and pre-planned attempt to attack me. The windshields of the vehicles were damaged and the CCTV wires had also been cut, so footage was also not available,” Kamble said.He added that he had no personal enmity with anyone and was unable to understand the motive behind the attack.Kamble subsequently lodged a complaint at Mundhwa police station. Police are examining CCTV footage from the surrounding area and other evidence to identify the suspects.An officer from the Mundhwa police said none of the other vehicles parked in the society were targeted and only Kamble’s two cars were vandalised.Kamble, a former MLA, served as minister in the BJP-led govt during Devendra Fadnavis’s first term from 2014 to 2019. He was later replaced by his younger brother, Sunil Kamble, who is currently serving his second term as BJP MLA from the Pune Cantonment constituency.Smita Wasnik, senior police inspector of the Mundhwa police, said a non-cognisable offence had been registered against unidentified persons based on Kamble’s complaint.“We have also checked CCTV footage from the surrounding areas. Further investigation is underway,” she said.
Article Summary: Two cars belonging to Dilip Kamble were vandalised by unidentified persons. Kamble said the vandalism appeared to be a deliberate and pre-planned attempt to target him. Police are examining CCTV footage from the surrounding area and other evidence to identify the suspects.

Article Title: Three young sisters, cousin die as bus collides with moped in Tamil Nadu
Article Text:
Four young girls died tragically after a college bus collided with their moped





NAMAKKAL: Three young sisters and their 11-year-old cousin riding on a moped died after a private college bus collided with their vehicle at Elachipalayam near Tiruchengode in Namakkal district on Thursday.The deceased were identified as S Kalaichelvi, 19, a second-year student at a government college; her sisters Nivedha, 15, a Class XI student, and Dhanushree, 11, a Class VII student; and their cousin R Abinaya, 11, a Class VI student. All four were residents of Sakkarampalayam.Kalaichelvi picked her sisters and Abinaya from their school near Elachipalayam and was returning home on the moped when the bus crashed into their two-wheeler. In the impact, all the four were thrown off the moped.While Kalaichelvi and Nivedha died on the spot, Dhanushree and Abinaya died on the way to a hospital, Elachipalayam police said.The bus belongs to a private educational institution near Rasipuram.Kalaichelvi, Nivedha and Dhanushree were daughters of vegetable traders Sekar and Amudha. Abinaya was the daughter of Sekar’s brother Rameshbabu and Vasantha. Elachipalayam police have registered a case.Meanwhile, bus driver Praveen, 30, of Rasipuram, surrendered at the Tiruchengode police station.Former district collector S Uma has been supporting Kalaichelvi’s education as her father is suffering from cancer.
Article Summary: Three young sisters and their 11-year-old cousin riding on a moped died after a private college bus collided with their vehicle. The deceased were identified as S Kalaichelvi, 19, a second-year student at a government college; her sisters Nivedha, 15, and Dhanushree, 11, a Class VII student.

Article Title: ‘Asked our community, then thrashed us again’: Journalists 'assaulted' at Delhi's Saket police station, cops deny
Article Text:
Two women YouTubers claim Delhi Police assaulted them after detention at Saket police station





NEW DELHI: Two women journalists and YouTubers alleged that they were detained and assaulted by Delhi Police personnel after attempting to question chief minister Rekha Gupta at an event in south Delhi on Thursday. Police denied the allegations, describing them as “factually incorrect” and “misleading”.According to the women, they had gone to cover the inauguration of a new wing at Max Hospital in Saket, attended by Union home minister Amit Shah and the Delhi chief minister. One of them alleged in a video circulated on social media that they were stopped while trying to question Gupta and taken to Saket police station.“We wanted to question the Delhi chief minister. But we were detained and brought to Saket Police Station. The police teams took us to a room, where they assaulted us brutally. They asked which community we belonged to and thrashed us again,” the journalist alleged.The women claimed they were taken to a room inside the police station, where they were assaulted and abused. They alleged that both sustained injuries during the incident. Videos showing the women displaying injury marks on different parts of their bodies were also circulated on social media, though the allegations could not be independently verified.Delhi Police rejected the accusations and gave a different account of the events, saying the women had obstructed a designated VVIP security route by parking their scooter near the venue.A senior police officer said the women were not carrying identity cards and were repeatedly asked to move their vehicle after being informed about the security arrangements. Police further alleged that they created a ruckus and manhandled a pregnant police officer.The women were subsequently taken to Saket police station for enquiry, police said, adding that they were free to leave within five to 10 minutes of reaching the station and were not restrained.“Nobody was holding their hands or preventing them from leaving, but they chose not to go,” an officer said.Deputy Commissioner of Police (South) Anant Mittal described claims that the women were assaulted for attempting to question the chief minister as “totally false, misleading and baseless” and urged people not to circulate unverified information.Meanwhile, several journalists’ organisations condemned the alleged assault and demanded a free and fair investigation.The Press Club of India, Indian Women’s Press Corps, Delhi Union of Journalists, Press Association and Kerala Union of Working Journalists, in a joint statement, alleged that the two freelance journalists were manhandled near the venue before being taken to Saket police station and assaulted there.The organisations demanded action against those responsible and urged Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar to order a fair probe. They also appealed to the Press Council of India to take suo motu cognisance of the matter.The Aam Aadmi Party also targeted the BJP-led Delhi government, with party leader Saurabh Bharadwaj alleging that the journalists were assaulted for asking questions of the chief minister.Delhi Police, however, maintained that the allegations were baseless and that the women were taken to the police station after they allegedly refused to comply with security instructions on the designated VVIP route.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Two women journalists and YouTubers claim Delhi Police assaulted them after detention at Saket police station. Police deny the allegations, describing them as “factually incorrect’ and “misleading’ Delhi Police said the women had obstructed a designated VVIP security route by parking their scooter near the venue.

Article Title: 'Nishu, I am with you': Rahul Gandhi backs Jantar Mantar protester who claimed her father was 'attacked' in CJP protests
Article Text:
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi(L), Nishu Aazad (R)

What Nishu Aazad alleged





NEW DELHI: Congress leader and LoP in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has backed Jantar Mantar protester Nishu Aazad after she accused the Delhi Police of failing to act against a man allegedly involved in an attack on her father during CJP protest, according to news agency ANI.Nishu Aazad had appealed to Rahul Gandhi for help, saying the police had not taken action despite an FIR being registered more than a month and a half ago. She also claimed that a video of the accused allegedly admitting to the assault was circulating online.Responding to her appeal on X, Rahul Gandhi said, "Nishu, there's no need to panic. I'm with you. It's clear that you're being targeted because you raise your voice for the rights of your community and students."The Congress leader also questioned the alleged inaction by the Delhi Police and criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah."Amit Shah's Delhi Police, on one hand, commits inhuman brutality against students. On the other hand, the criminal who smashed the head of a Dalit girl's father is roaming freely in the open. Narendra Modi ji, Amit Shah ji—Why does such a criminal have the protection of you and the people in your party? Will there be action now, or will you keep shielding someone?" Gandhi wrote, concluding his post with "Jai Bhim.Jai Constitution. "Nishu Aazad had earlier posted a video seeking help from Rahul Gandhi. She alleged that her father was attacked by Swatantra Bhardwaj and suffered a head injury that required stitches.She claimed a video showing Bhardwaj allegedly admitting to the assault had been widely circulated."A video of Swatantra Bhardwaj is circulating throughout the country in which he himself is accepting that he hit my father's head and should be charged under Section 307 for attempted murder. When he hit my father's head and my father had to get stitches, we filed an FIR against him. But the police are not doing anything. It's been more than a month and a half. The police are not doing anything. They are fooling us and keeping us busy in the name of medical examinations. My hope from the Delhi Police is completely broken now. Now my only hope is from Rahul Gandhi ji. I believe you will help me get justice," Aazad said in her post.Nishu Aazad also questioned why those accused of crimes could continue to remain free despite allegedly showing no fear of the law."I want to know how people who have no fear of the law can walk free. They should be behind bars, especially those who proudly boast about their crimes instead of accepting their mistakes. So, I really request you, Rahul Gandhi ji, I need your help. Please help me get justice," she urged.
Article Summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi backs Jantar Mantar protester Nishu Aazad. She accused the Delhi Police of failing to act against a man allegedly involved in an attack on her father during CJP protest. She also claimed that a video of the accused allegedly admitting to the assault was circulating online.
