Article Title: Gogi 2.0? Ankit Balyan murder brings gang back on Delhi Police radar
Article Text:
Haryanvi singer and Youtube Ankit Balyan

Delhi's underworld overhaul





NEW DELHI: The echo of gunfire outside a gym in UP’s Shamli on Aug 26 did more than just silence 27-year-old Haryanvi singer and YouTuber Ankit Balyan. It marked the revival of Delhi’s most feared Gogi gang, suggesting the syndicate remains active five years after kingpin Jitender Maan alias Gogi’s assassination in a crowded Rohini courtroom.Despite its core leadership — Rohit Moi, Deepak Boxer , Dinesh Karala, Yogesh Tunda and Deepak Teetar — in Tihar, the gang has managed to come out of the shadows with Balyan’s killing, ringing alarm bells in Delhi, with cops keeping a cautious watch on the developments. Specialised units have been roped in for a manhunt for the absconding shooters in the Balyan case amid fears they can strike in the city next, engage in extortion bids and kill rivals, according to sources.The gang’s resurgence is particularly alarming given that it has suffered massive setbacks. Besides the kingpin’s killing, the other gang members have been regularly arrested in Delhi and Haryana in the past two-three years. The rival Tajpuria gang dealt further blows with two back-to-back killings of Gogi’s henchmen earlier this year in outer Delhi. But the cartel’s hierarchy seems to have mutated rather than collapsed.So, how did the gang manage a comeback? Investigators suspect low-rung foot soldiers on bail and foreign-based handlers like Rahul alias Bholu Shahpuria helped the gang emerge from the shadows again. Also, the gang’s incarcerated bigwigs still seem to be active while in jail. A critical catalyst for the renewed aggression seems to be a strategic underworld alliance with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, forged years ago by Jitender Gogi himself.Supported by Lawrence’s overarching umbrella, the gang now relies on an expendable army of low-rung foot soldiers who are being allegedly recruited through Instagram and promised an “out of country” card after successful completion of tasks. The two absconding shooters in the Balyan case, it is suspected, may have fled abroad too. These street-level operatives are allegedly being coordinated by fugitive entities operating safely from foreign soil. Figures like Bholu Shahpuria, based in Canada, have stepped in to manage logistics.What has alarmed Delhi cops further is the apparent trigger in Balyan’s killing, which underscores the syndicate’s obsession with retribution. Balyan was allegedly a target for a music video featuring the lyrics “Bhari court me goli maarenge meri jaan”, with visual references to shooters dressed as lawyers. “The Gogi gang perceived the track as a direct insult mocking Gogi’s 2021 courtroom killing. The ‘insult’ was further magnified by the fact that Balyan shared the same local roots as Gogi’s rival, Tillu Tajpuria,” said an investigator.For years, Delhi witnessed a slew of killings — at least 36 murders in the past 15 years — in the gang war between Gogi and Tajpuria. Retired officials said this rivalry began one and a half decades ago as a college election dispute between childhood friends Gogi and Tajpuria morphed into a turf war.After Gogi’s killing, Deepak Boxer took the reins and ran the gang from Mexico, but he was tracked down and brought back after a complex operation by FBI and Delhi Police in April 2023.The Gogi gang extracted vengeance a month later when incarcerated loyalists — led by Yogesh Tunda and Deepak Titar — cornered Tillu Tajpuria inside Tihar Jail’s courtyard and stabbed him over 100 times with makeshift shivs.
Article Summary: Ankit Balyan's killing marks revival of Delhi's most feared Gogi gang. Specialised units have been roped in for a manhunt for the absconding shooters. Investigators suspect low-rung foot soldiers on bail and foreign-based handlers helped gang emerge from shadows.

Article Title: Worm in egg sets off food safety check at Mangaluru quick-commerce hub
Article Text:
Food safety officials inspected a quick-commerce facility in Mangaluru after a consumer complaint.





MANGALURU: A complaint about a worm allegedly found inside an egg delivered to a consumer has prompted food safety officials to inspect a quick-commerce facility in the city and temporarily seal its storage room.The consumer had approached health minister U T Khader, alleging that some of the eggs purchased through an online delivery platform were damaged and that a worm was found inside one of them.Acting on the complaint, food safety officials inspected the online retail facility at Falnir Square in Falnir area on Thursday. They found packets containing broken eggs at the facility and directed the personnel concerned to remove and dispose of them immediately.The storage room was also temporarily closed and sealed as a precautionary measure to facilitate cleaning and sanitisation of the food storage area, an official release said.The department will issue a notice to the establishment seeking an explanation for the incident. Further action will be decided based on the inspection findings and the facility management’s response, officials said.
Article Summary: Consumer complained that some eggs purchased through an online delivery platform were damaged and that a worm was found inside one of them. Food safety officials inspected the online retail facility at Falnir Square in Falnir area on Thursday. They found packets containing broken eggs at the facility and directed the personnel concerned to remove and dispose of them immediately.

Article Title: 1,000 Vidya Bharati schools in Bengal within a year, says CM Suvendu Adhikari
Article Text:
West Bengal's Chief Minister urged Vidya Bharati to establish one thousand new schools.

By: Subhajoy Roy

TOI





KOLKATA: Every district, municipality and panchayat in the state should host a school by Vidya Bharati, the education wing of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), CM Suvendu Adhikari said on Thursday and set a target of establishing at least 1,000 such institutions in Bengal within the next year.The CM invited the Vidya Bharati leadership to meet the entire education department at the state secretariat and added that Vidya Bharati must take responsibility for imparting nationalistic learning. Adhikari was speaking at an event to mark the 74th year of Vidya Bharati at Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture in Golpark.Bengal currently has 313 Vidya Bharati schools. Nationally, Vidya Bharati runs over 12,000 schools and 10,000 Bal Sanskar Kendras.Adhikari also signalled the merger of state’s four education departments — school education, higher education, technical and minority education — to establish a single department. “Our belief is to have a single education department. There will be no madrassa education department and others. You keep watching,” he said and added that the previous govt had polluted the state’s education environment and Vidya Bharati’s “help will be needed to come out of this”.He insisted Vidya Bharati should set up more schools in Murshidabad and South 24 Parganas, where “more anti-national activities take place”.Anand Rao, an official of Vidya Bharati, toldtheir schools train students in “bharatiyatwa (Indianness)” as well as puja rituals. “There are 313 schools in Bengal. Some are till class 5 and some till classes 8, 10 and 12,” he said. There are also 150 Sanskar Kendras where students learn puja rituals and about Indian culture and tradition.The website of Vidya Bharati Akhil Bhartiya Shiksha Sansthan says its vision is “to develop a national system of education which would help build a younger generation which is committed to Hindutva and infused with patriotic fervour”.The CM accused the previous Trinamool govt of deliberately and strategically twisting the Bengali syllabus in schools to divide Bengali-speaking people.“Mother was referred to as ‘amma’ and not ‘ma’. Similarly, the sky was referred to as ‘asman’ and not ‘akash’. Bengali language was distorted in a planned manner. The syllabus was created in such a way that Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar’s or Swami Vivekananda’s lessons remained neglected. Division was created in the minds of children through such distortion of language,” he alleged.Adhikari said Syama Prasad Mookerjee’s call of ‘ek desh, ek bidhan, ek nishan, ek pradhan’ would apply to education as well. “We will not allow an arrangement where the higher education department will look after all universities while another department will look after Aliah University,” he said. Aliah University is managed by Bengal govt’s minority affairs department.“I felicitated the board toppers. Later the minority affairs department sent a separate file for felicitating 27 Muslim students. I asked why? Students do not have religion. I have already felicitated 20 students and they include Muslims, Jaina, Buddhists,” he said.Adhikari added that he had seen a video where a student, who wore a tilak on his head, was forced to wipe it off in school. He did not name the school. He added that the govt knew how to overcome opposition to singing Vande Mataram in schools. “Some were saying they will not sing it. I said we will stop funds. Then they agreed to sing. Still they were not moving their lips. I told the education secretary that they will have to sing ‘tomari murti gori mandir e mandir e’ (we build your idols in temples),” he said.The CM added that he had also requested Union defence minister Rajnath Singh to establish more Sainik schools in the state. “Rajnath ji was in Kolkata recently. I said give Bengal more Sainik schools. I told him that I will write to you to introduce NCC in each school. I have already sent the letters. Vidya Bharati can help with these. We will work together,” he added.
Article Summary: Bengal currently has 313 Vidya Bharati schools. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari set a target of establishing at least 1,000 such institutions in Bengal within the next year. He also signalled the merger of state’s four education departments.

Article Title: Fire breaks out at Maharashtra's Asian Hospital; over 50 patients, including 9 infants rescued
Article Text:
Fire erupted at Asian Hospital in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar early Friday morning





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: A major fire broke out at Asian Hospital in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar around 2.30 am on Friday, triggering panic among patients, relatives and hospital staff.According to Fire Brigade officials, around 58 patients were admitted to the hospital when the blaze broke out, including nine newborns in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU). All patients were safely evacuated in a swift operation.No patient or hospital staff member was injured, officials said.Thick smoke engulfed parts of the building, prompting hospital staff to raise the alarm and alert the Fire Brigade. Three fire tenders were rushed to the spot, and firefighters began efforts to bring the blaze under control.The incident caused panic among relatives, with several of them rushing to the hospital after learning about the fire. Police personnel also reached the spot and cordoned off the area.The exact cause of the fire was not immediately known, though a short circuit is suspected to have triggered the blaze.
Article Summary: Fire broke out at Asian Hospital in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar around 2.30 am on Friday. Around 58 patients were admitted to the hospital when the blaze broke out, including nine newborns in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) All patients were safely evacuated in a swift operation.

Article Title: Watch: Stray dogs save mentally ill woman from sexual assault attempt in Coimbatore
Article Text:
Stray dogs intervened to save a mentally ill woman from an alleged assault





COIMBATORE: A pack of stray dogs saved a mentally ill woman from an alleged sexual assault attempt by an intoxicated youth near Thudiyalur in Coimbatore during the early hours of Friday. The entire incident was captured on CCTV, and police have arrested the suspect.The incident took place around 2 am near the railway overbridge in the NGGO Colony-Ashokapuram area near Thudiyalur. A mentally ill woman, who routinely stays in the area, was sitting by the roadside when a youth, allegedly intoxicated, approached her.According to CCTV footage, two stray dogs that stay near the woman began barking continuously as the youth approached. The youth asked the woman if the dogs belonged to her. The woman reportedly replied that he should throw a stone to scare them away.The youth threw a stone, driving the dogs back a few paces, but the animals continued to stay nearby and bark at him.Taking advantage of the isolated spot, the intoxicated youth allegedly attempted to sexually assault the woman. When she began screaming for help, one of the stray dogs immediately lunged at the assailant.The dogs barked furiously, bit the attacker and grabbed his legs, pulling him away from the woman.Overpowered by the animals, the youth abandoned his attempt and fled the scene, with the dogs chasing him away. Thudiyalur police identified and arrested the suspect.
Article Summary: A pack of stray dogs saved a mentally ill woman from an alleged sexual assault attempt by an intoxicated youth. The incident took place near the railway overbridge in the NGGO Colony-Ashokapuram area near Thudiyalur. The entire incident was captured on CCTV, and police have arrested the suspect.

Article Title: Not given FIR copy, says ex-bureaucrat Ashish Joshi; no need at this stage, say cops
Article Text:
Ex-bureaucrat Ashish Joshi





NEW DELHI: Former bureaucrat Ashish Joshi , who was questioned by Delhi Police 's special cell for several hours Wednesday, said he and his lawyers were yet to be pro-vided with a copy of the FIR against him.Speaking to TOI, Joshi, a 1992-batch officer of the Indian Post and Telecommunication Accounts and Finance Service, said he went to Delhi Police headquarters Thursday with a letter from his lawyers asking that he be provided with a copy of the FIR against him. The FIR has been registered under section 192 of Bharatiya Nyay Sanhita, which relates to "wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause riot".Joshi said he was approached by two Delhi Police officers as he was leaving Nehru Park Wednesday morning."They showed me the first page of the FIR for a short while. It mentioned a post I had made on X on Aug 26 about SIR and elections in West Bengal. I was not shown the second page of the FIR; so, I am at the police headquarters with a letter from my lawyers to seek a copy, which they are required to provide to me," Joshi said.Police sources said as Joshi was not arrested and only questioned, there was no need to provide a copy of the FIR at this stage.Sources said that the cops questioned him regarding his post on X that called for "Nuremberg style trial" - military tribunals held after World War II - of the chief election commission in connection with the West Bengal elections while demanding that they be held again.During questioning, Joshi claimed, he was asked about his social media activity, including his post on the chief election commissioner and another he made on Aug 13.Earlier in the day, Joshi posted on X that he was not allowed to inform his family and friends that he was being questioned by police offi-cials Wednesday."Informing an individual's family during interrogation or detention is a legal mandate, not an optional courtesy... I was only permitted to make a call at 6.38pm, leaving my family & friends in total panic the entire day," he posted on X, tagging Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar.Delhi Police, however, rejected the allegations, asserting that all mandated legal provisions were followed during the questioning. Police said that following their request to join the investigation, Joshi came to the special cell's office in New Friends Colony in his own vehicle and was escorted home safely and cordially in the evening.Sources in Delhi Police had said Wednesday that Joshi and his wife were duly informed about the questioning and the registration of an FIR.
Article Summary: Ex-bureaucrat Ashish Joshi was questioned by Delhi Police's special cell for several hours Wednesday. Joshi, a 1992-batch officer of the Indian Post and Telecommunication Accounts and Finance Service, said he and his lawyers were yet to be pro-vided with a copy of the FIR.

Article Title: ‘World has reached the moon, we still carry children’: 80-year wait for bridge in Chhattisgarh's Sonpal village
Article Text:
In Sonpal village, daily life is disrupted by the absence of a crucial bridge





RAIPUR: “The world has reached the moon, but we still carry our children on our shoulders across the stream to help them reach school.” That is how residents of remote Sonpal village in Durgukondal block of Kanker district describe an eight-decade wait for a bridge they say has been promised by successive governments but never built.For villagers, the missing bridge is not merely an infrastructure gap. During the rains, it determines whether children can reach school, whether families can travel for work or treatment, and whether anyone can cross the village boundary without risking a fall into the swollen stream.Videos of parents carrying children on their shoulders through the flooded crossing have surfaced on social media, drawing attention to the village’s daily struggle.One of the women said villagers had even travelled to the state capital with applications seeking a bridge, but nothing changed. “It feels as if we are still not part of independent India,” she said.“The four months of monsoon are the worst. If someone falls ill, an ambulance cannot reach us. Children miss school, and sometimes their books get washed away in the water,” she said. “How are our children supposed to go to school? If they have to attend, the only option is for parents to carry them on their shoulders, otherwise their uniforms get soaked and covered in mud.They fall and others are so short, they can't stand in that water. Who would understand our pain? A bridge has to be built here.”Village head Sanuram Dugga said generations have lived with the same demand. “Our fathers and grandfathers kept asking for this bridge and died waiting. Now our generation is asking for it,” he said. “Governments come and go— everyone said it would be built. The promises were made, not the bridge.”A 2.3km blacktop road, constructed about three years ago at a cost of crores, exists on both sides of the stream. But in between, the road gets inundated during the monsoon.During the monsoon, villagers say adults wade across at considerable risk, while younger children are carried on shoulders or backs to get them safely to the other side.Women in the village — Iswanti Rana, Subhadra Patel, Sagro Bai Dugga, Basanti Kumeti and Somari Yadav — said they have heard the same assurance since they got married in Sonpal: “The bridge will be built this year.” Now, their children are bearing the brunt.Residents say the absence of a crossing affects not only schoolchildren but anyone needing to reach markets, hospitals, workplaces or government offices outside the village.Mahendra Singh Thakur, a sub-engineer with the Bridge Corporation in Kanker, told reporters that the Sonpal bridge has been included in the 2026-27 budget and that a fresh estimate will now be prepared and forwarded for further action.For Sonpal, however, an estimate is still not a bridge.
Article Summary: In Sonpal village, daily life is disrupted by the absence of a crucial bridge. During the rains, it determines whether children can reach school, whether families can travel for work or treatment, and whether anyone can cross the village boundary without risking a fall into the swollen stream.

Article Title: Anna Hazare health update: Stable, eating and drinking comfortably, says doctor
Article Text:
Anna Hazare has been kept in a special ward room and does not require intensive care, the doctor said.

(With agency inputs)





MUMBAI: Social activist Anna Hazare has been admitted to Bombay Hospital in Mumbai after his health deteriorated following a month-long bout of viral fever and recurring loose stools, a doctor told news agency ANI.Dr Gautam Bhansali, consultant physician and infectious disease specialist, said Hazare was admitted to the hospital on Monday night and is currently under his care.Hazare had earlier been receiving treatment at a hospital in Shirur, near Ralegan Siddhi.However, doctors decided to shift him to Bombay Hospital for further evaluation after his infection worsened and showed signs of beginning to affect his kidneys.“He had been suffering from a viral fever for about a month and had also experienced bouts of loose stools,” Bhansali said.The doctor said Hazare had been in and out of the Shirur hospital during this period. Following a slight worsening of the infection and concerns over its possible impact on his kidneys, he was brought to Bombay Hospital for detailed investigations and treatment."Consequently, he had been in and out of the hospital in Shirur.When the infection worsened slightly—and there were indications that it was beginning to affect his kidneys—it was decided to move him to Bombay Hospital for further testing, "the doctor said.At the time of admission, Hazare was stable, although he was experiencing weakness and fatigue. He has since been started on appropriate treatment and is showing significant improvement, the doctor said."At the time of admission, he was completely stable, though he was experiencing some weakness and fatigue. We have since initiated the appropriate treatment, and he is showing significant improvement and responding well to the therapy. He has been placed in a special ward room; there was no need to admit him to the ICU, " the doctor added.Hazare has been kept in a special ward room and does not require intensive care, Bhansali said.Doctors have conducted tests including a 2D echocardiogram and are carrying out further investigations, including urine tests and screenings for infections. The reports are expected within the next three to four days, following which doctors will decide on the further course of treatment.“He is eating and drinking comfortably and is stable,” Bhansali said.The doctor also said Maharashtra chief minister had called after Hazare was admitted to enquire about his health. The chief minister also spoke to doctors on Tuesday to seek an update on his condition.
Article Summary: Hazare had earlier been receiving treatment at a hospital in Shirur, near Ralegan Siddhi. Doctors decided to shift him to Bombay Hospital for further evaluation. Hazare has been kept in a special ward room and does not require intensive care, the doctor said.

Article Title: Bus fresh from repairs, no passengers aboard: How UP teen was lured, gang-raped and dumped in Delhi
Article Text:
The sleeper bus had curtains around its berths, which police said allegedly helped the accused conceal what was happening inside during the journey.

Wrong stop amid rain and darkness

Curtains drawn as bus moves

Bus was heading to Timarpur after repairs

(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)





NEW DELHI: A family row, a wrong stop, and an empty bus returning from a repair workshop set off a chain of events that ended in the alleged gang-rape of a 16-year-old girl from Uttar Pradesh, police said on Monday.Stranded amid heavy rain and darkness after getting off at the wrong stop, the teenager was allegedly gang-raped inside a moving sleeper bus after boarding the vehicle seeking help, police said. The bus then travelled nearly 47km before the teenager was allegedly abandoned near Kashmere Gate.The incident took place on the night of August 4 after the teenager, from Mainpuri district, left home following a disagreement with her family and set out to meet her cousin in Noida.According to police, the girl got off at Pari Chowk by mistake amid heavy rain and darkness. An empty sleeper bus passing through the area stopped after she signalled for help.The driver, Kuldeep, and conductor, Sandeep, allegedly told her that the bus was headed towards Noida Sector 63 and allowed her to board.Police said the conductor allegedly began making obscene advances towards the teenager soon after the bus started moving.The girl, in her complaint, alleged that both the driver and conductor subsequently raped her and threatened to kill her when she resisted.The sleeper bus had curtains around its berths, which police said allegedly helped the accused conceal what was happening inside during the journey.The bus travelled nearly 47km towards Kashmere Gate. The accused allegedly abandoned the teenager on Ring Road near the Kashmere Gate bus terminal late at night and fled.The terrified student approached Kashmere Gate police and reported the incident.Police subsequently arrested Kuldeep and Sandeep from a bus parking area in Timarpur and seized the sleeper bus. The vehicle has been sent for forensic examination.Police said the bus had earlier broken down and was taken to a workshop in Surajpur for repairs. After the repairs were completed, the driver and conductor were taking the empty bus to Timarpur when they encountered the teenager at Pari Chowk.Monu Gupta, manager of the bus travel company, said the bus had been parked at Himgiri, Surajpur, from July 27 to August 4 for repair work due to a sensor-related issue."We had asked the driver and conductor to take the bus to Timarpur for repair. The next morning, we received a call from the administration, we were told that the bus had been seized and the driver and conductor were arrested," Gupta said.Recounting the bus's movements, Gupta said the vehicle was taken out of Himgiri around 5pm on August 4 after the repairs were completed. The driver and conductor later moved it out again around 9pm and were instructed to proceed towards Timarpur."We had parked the car in Himgiri to repair it. When it was repaired on the 4th of August, we took the car from there. We took the car out of Himgiri at 5 in the evening." "After that, they parked the car a little further from there. They took the car out at 9. After taking the car out at 9, we told them to go to Timarpur."Gupta said the company expected the bus to reach Timarpur but instead received a call from Delhi authorities the following morning informing them that the vehicle had been seized. Further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: A 16-year-old girl from Uttar Pradesh was allegedly gang-raped inside a moving sleeper bus. The bus had broken down and was taken to a workshop in Surajpur for repairs. After the repairs were completed, the driver and conductor were taking the empty bus to Timarpur. They encountered the teenager at Pari Chowk amid heavy rain and darkness.
